title: Renewal Outcomes Playbook + Deck Bundle
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, modular deck + playbook designed for mid‑cycle QBRs and renewal conversations. The artifact intentionally mixes an executive-focused slide path (2–6 slides) and a technical/operational appendix (dive slides and service health dashboards) so CSMs can tailor presentation length to audience.

Status / usage notes:
- Draft: internal testing with two pilot accounts (RetailCo, FinPro).
- Intention: replace 3 internal ad-hoc decks with a single bundle that scales from 'health check' syncs to full renewal negotiation.
- Feedback loop: collect comments in Confluence page CONFLUENCE-1234, tag suggestions with #deck-feedback.

High-level structure (pick subset based on audience):
1) Executive opener (1 slide): current partnership headline + Renewal ask/next-step placeholder
2) Outcomes & value map (1–2 slides): business metrics tied to our product value (top KPIs by customer)
3) Adoption & ROI narrative (1–2 slides): feature adoption, time-to-value stories, cost savings examples
4) Health & risk (1 slide): product health signals + renewal risk score and rationale
5) Renewal options (1 slide): standard vs enterprise variants + recommended path and timeline
6) Ask & commitments (1 slide): customer commitments, Redwood commitments, decision points and dates
Appendix: operational metrics, incident timeline, workplan, deep technical notes

Slide-by-slide: speaker notes and placeholders
- Title / opener:
  - Slide title: Partnership Snapshot — [Quarter].
  - Placeholder bullets: "Top impact: X% decrease in latency, Y M tokens saved/mon"; "Big win: Customer engineering migration to dedicated cluster"
  - Speaker prompt: "Quick headline: what moved the needle in the last 90 days? Two minutes, no org chart deep dive."

- Outcomes & value map:
  - Visual: 3-column mapping: Business Goal | Redwood Feature | Measurable Metric (KPI + delta).
  - Placeholder KPI examples: "Support deflection %", "Content generation throughput", "Avg latency (ms) for 95th pct".
  - Data sources: "rush: query GA/Amplitude/Datadog -> metrics snippet. TODO: add SQL for 'tokens_by_route'"

- Adoption & ROI narrative (standard vs enterprise):
  - Standard audience: highlight time saved, number of users, API calls growth. Keep simple.
  - Enterprise audience: add security/compliance value, dedicated capacity hours, SLA attainment numbers.
  - Speaker prompt: "Tell 1 short customer story (engineering or PM testimonial)."

- Health & risk slide (this is the single most sensitive slide):
  - Elements: renewal risk score (0–100), contributing factors (usage drop, errors, executive churn, unmet feature requests), recommended mitigations.
  - Risk scoring rubric (useful quick model; simple arithmetic):
    - Usage trend (-40 to +40): >10% decline in last 30d = -30, stable = 0, strong growth = +20
    - SLA/Incidents (-30 to 0): major incident in last 90d = -30, minor = -10, none = 0
    - Exec engagement (-20 to +20): exec sponsor active = +15, neutral = 0, churn risk = -20
    - Contract size/strategic weight (-10 to +30): enterprise anchor account = +25, small commercial = 0
    - Final score = sum (clamp to -100..100) then map to bands: red (<-20), amber (-20..10), green (>10)
  - TODO: automate this score with a weekly script (JIRA-CUST-987).

- Renewal options slide (standard + enterprise variations):
  - Format: 3-column table (Offering | What's changing | Recommended for).
  - Example rows (placeholders):
    - Standard: monthly hosted API, pay-as-you-go pricing, best for small teams or pilots
    - Dedicated: reserved GPU capacity, committed throughput, SLAs, best for predictable production workloads
    - Enterprise: private deployment (VPC), audit logs, long-term support, custom SSO/KMS integration
  - Pricing signal: provide ballpark uplift percentages (example: Dedicated = +30% unit cost vs hosted for latency guarantees; Enterprise = custom) — mark as "estimate"

- Ask & commitments slide:
  - Decision timeline (recommended): Placeholder dates for negotiation, PO issuance, transition kickoff.
  - Mutual commitments: e.g., Redwood: rollout plan + 60d migration support; Customer: finalize SSO, designate PO owner.

Appendix (technical & operational deep dives) — include as collapsible slides for technical stakeholders:
- Service health dashboard snippets (Datadog charts): 95th/99th latency, error rate, GPU utilization, prefix cache hit rate
- Incident timeline & remediation status (last 6 months)
- Workplan for next 90 days (epics, owners, acceptance criteria)
- Technical blockers & asks (data residency, model quantization support, custom tokenization)

Renewal tracker template (tabular rows to paste into a sheet or slide table):
- Column headers: account, ARR, renewal_date, current_tier, renewal_owner, risk_score, next_meeting_date, action_items, blockers, notes
- Example row (text to paste):
  - RetailCo | $280k | 2025-06-15 | Dedicated | Priya Shah | 12 (Amber) | 2025-04-02 | align exec on ROI dashboard; schedule migration kickoff | waiting on legal redlines

Playbook: sequence for a typical enterprise renewal (90–120 day runway)
1) 90d out: enable renewal tracker row, initial internal sync (owner + solutions engineer + CSM).
2) 60d out: executive briefing (use executive opener + outcomes slides).
3) 45d out: proposal delivery (include clear options and recommended path).
4) 30d out: negotiation & technical readiness checks (appendix review with infra team).
5) 7–14d out: legal & procurement finalization.
6) Post-sign: onboarding/migration kickoff within 14 business days.

Escalation lanes & playbook notes:
- If risk_score <= -20 and ARR > $100k: escalate to CS Lead and AE; schedule emergency exec sync within 7 days.
- If technical blocker prevents migration: open a "migration-blocker" ticket in Jira and tag eng-sre; assign a war room owner.

Talk tracks / sample language (CSM)
- Executive summary opener: "Over the last 90 days we've reduced average inference latency by X% for your production routes, which directly shortened checkout times and improved conversion by Y points. We're recommending Dedicated for predictable scale and a 12-month commitment to lock in price."
- When facing price pushback: "We can pilot a dedicated pool for 30 days at no additional commitment so you can validate latency and throughput before committing; we can then convert to committed capacity in your renewal."

Work-in-progress TODOs (internal):
- [ ] Add SQL snippets for tokens_by_route and adoption_by_team
- [ ] Plug in retail benchmark numbers (RetailCo pilot) into outcomes slide
- [ ] Confirm legal timeline estimates with finance (Priya)
- [ ] Create an automated weekly risk_score report (owner: Diego)

Appendix: file/asset list to attach to the deck when exporting
- PDF export of Datadog dashboards (last 90 days)
- CSV of API usage by route (3 months)
- SLA attainment report (monthly roll-up)
- Technical architecture diagram for Dedicated/Private variants

Notes on tailoring (quick guide for CSMs):
- Short exec-only meeting (10–15m): use slides 1,2,6 only.
- Technical stakeholder deep-dive (60m): use full deck + appendix.
- Commercial negotiation (30–45m): use outcomes, renewal options, and ask + pricing appendix.

Last words:
This file should live alongside customer notes for each account. The goal is to reduce ad-hoc decks and create one reusable bundle that can be rapidly personalized. Please add after-action notes in the Confluence page and drop feedback in #cs-renewals.
